newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS - Miner fears red tape may tie up Czech gold.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Miner fears red tape may tie up Czech gold.

text.p: Canadian mining company TVX Gold Inc said on Wednesday it had trebled its estimate of gold in the Czech Republic's Kasperske Hory deposits, but that local bureacracy may mean the region's riches go untapped.
"The current estimates of the geological sources of gold in Kasperske Hory have, with investigations still to be completed, been raised to three million ounces (100 tonnes)," TVX said in a statement.

TVX Bohemia Dulni a.s., a wholly-owned subsidiary of TVX Gold, acquired a six-year exploration licence from the Czech government in 1993 for the scenic Kasperske Hory area in the Sumava mountains which border Austria and Germany.

But since then, the company has been under attack by environmental campaigners, had its licence suspended by the Environment Ministry and, most recently, seen exploration halted because of opposition from local landowners.
Despite the potentially huge rewards, TVX Gold vice chairman John Hick told Reuters his company's patience would not last forever.

"Obviously you don't indefinitely throw money at something," he said. "This is a substantial resource, it's an interesting resource and it would be a shame for the company and the country if it doesn't go ahead in the proper fashion."
Following a vocal campaign by environmentalists and the Kasperske Hory local council, landowners in the region have refused to grant rights of access.

Campaigners say that recovering the gold would do irreparable harm to an area of great natural beauty. Gold has been mined in the region for centuries but mining was deemed inefficient and stopped in the 1930s.
TVX has responded by pledging to use the latest cyanide-free methods to recover gold from ore.
The matter has been referred to the district authority but Hick said he was worried that local officials were shying away from taking a decision on the politically sensitive issue.

"There's nothing wrong with the mining law here. It's very normal and we knew the procedures when we came in. What's happening is that some of the procedures aren't being followed by some of the people in the system," he added.
TVX's problems highlight the difficulty of assessing investment risk in even the most advanced of the post-communist countries where laws can change faster than attitudes.

While the Czech Republic is crying out for more direct investment to rejuvenate its dilapidated industry, western companies frequently complain of excessive red tape and sometimes hostility to foreigners from Czech officials.
Czechs are wary of allowing strategic assets to fall into foreign hands.
Hick cautioned that the kind of treatment meted out to his company could hold foreign investors back.

"Prime Minister Klaus is going to Canada and one of the main reasons is to encourage foreign investors into the Czech Republic. Well, you don't encourage it by having situations like this," said Hick.

Even if TVX's problems are quickly overcome it will be years before gold mining begins in Kasperske Hory. When exploration has been finally completed, the company will do a feasibility study and apply for a mining licence from the government.
